back: 1) Trend by centered moving average. 2) Detrend. 3) Average per position of the period and center. 4) Remainder.

front: Why does the trend window equal one full period?
back: A window of one full period contains each seasonal position once, so the seasonal highs and lows cancel and only the trend remains.

front: How does the trend step change for an even period?
back: Use the 2×m average: a window of m+1 values with half weight on both end values. The first and last m/2 trend values are NaN.

front: How do you center the seasonal indexes?
back: Additive: subtract their mean, so they sum to 0. Multiplicative: divide by their mean, so they average 1.

front: What does STL add to classical decomposition?
back: Loess smoothing: the seasonal pattern can change slowly, the trend reaches both ends, and a robust option reduces the effect of outliers.

front: Why is a centered-average trend risky as a model feature?
back: It uses values after time t, so it leaks the future. Use decomposition to describe the past.
